content: The CIDB assigns contractors a grade from 1 to 9 based on their financial capability and their track record of completed projects. The process of upgrading a CIDB grade is arduous; it requires the successful completion of projects of a certain size and demonstrating sufficient available capital and financial stability. This creates a classic "chicken-and-egg" problem: to win large contracts, you need a high CIDB grade, but to get a high CIDB grade, you need to have completed large contracts.
